name: Real Madrid
description: The Santiago Bernabéu is an 81,044-seat footballing temple in the heart of Madrid that has hosted five UEFA Champions League finals and stands as the definitive symbol of Real Madrid's century of dominance. Completely redeveloped between 2019 and 2023, the stadium features a retractable roof and a striking 360-degree illuminated titanium facade, making it one of the most spectacular sporting venues on the planet.

name: FC Barcelona
description: Camp Nou is the largest football stadium in Europe, a 99,354-seat colossus in the Les Corts district of Barcelona that has been FC Barcelona's spiritual home since 1957. Emerging from the landmark Espai Barça renovation with a stunning translucent roof and modernised facilities, it reclaims its place as one of the world's most iconic and atmospheric sporting arenas.

name: Atlético de Madrid
description: The Cívitas Metropolitano is a sweeping 68,456-seat elliptical arena in the east of Madrid that opened in 2017 and hosted the UEFA Champions League final just two years later. Its continuous roof, steep stands, and the ferocious noise generated by the colchonero faithful combine to make it one of the most intimidating home fortresses in European football.

name: Athletic Club
description: Known as La Catedral, San Mamés is a spectacular 53,289-seat stadium in Bilbao that opened in 2013 on the site of the club's cherished original ground, honouring its predecessor while setting a new benchmark in modern stadium design. The steeply raked, compact stands bring supporters close to the action and amplify the fierce Basque pride of a fanbase whose devotion to their uniquely local club is unlike anything else in football.

name: Villarreal CF
description: The Estadio de la Cerámica is a compact 23,500-seat arena in the small city of Villarreal that belies its modest size with a remarkable European pedigree earned through consistent appearances in UEFA competition. Named after the ceramics industry that defines the region, the stadium's famous Yellow Submarine atmosphere and the tight proximity of its passionate fans to the pitch make it one of La Liga's most characterful grounds.

name: Real Betis
description: The Estadio Benito Villamarín is a 60,720-seat icon in the Heliópolis district of Seville that has stood as Real Betis's proud home since 1929, repeatedly modernised while retaining its grand old-school grandeur. The fierce devotion of the Béticos creates one of Spanish football's most passionate atmospheres, which reaches its ferocious peak during the intense cross-city derby against rivals Sevilla.

name: Real Sociedad
description: The Reale Arena is a 39,500-seat stadium in the heart of San Sebastián that was extensively rebuilt between 2016 and 2019 to bring the stands dramatically closer to the pitch and transform the match-day atmosphere. Set against the green Basque hills with the river Urumea nearby, it offers a modern yet fiercely authentic experience that reflects the independent spirit of Basque football culture.

name: Sevilla FC
description: The Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán is a 43,883-seat fortress in central Seville, opened in 1958 and long regarded as one of the most intimidating grounds in Spanish football thanks to its steep, close-set stands and the relentless noise of the sevillista faithful. As the home of the most decorated club in UEFA Europa League history, it has witnessed countless legendary European nights that have cemented Seville's status as a major continental football city.

name: RC Celta de Vigo
description: Estadio Abanca-Balaídos is a 29,000-seat historic ground on Spain's Atlantic coast in the Galician city of Vigo, first opened in 1928 and substantially expanded with new stands built for the 1982 FIFA World Cup. The notoriously wet Galician climate, the passionate and vocal Celta supporters, and the stadium's distinctive multi-era architecture combine to create one of La Liga's most atmospheric and memorable match-day experiences.

name: CA Osasuna
description: El Sadar is a tightly packed 23,576-seat stadium in the ancient Navarrese capital of Pamplona where the club's famously loyal fanbase have supported Osasuna through triumph and adversity since the original ground opened in 1967. The modern covered bowl, completed in its current form in 2020, traps noise to create an intensity of atmosphere that makes Osasuna one of the toughest home environments to visit anywhere in La Liga.

name: Getafe CF
description: The Coliseum Alfonso Pérez is a 17,393-seat ground in the industrial city of Getafe, south of Madrid, that has been the club's home since 1998 and is renowned for generating an atmosphere that far exceeds what its modest size might suggest. With the stadium embedded in a working-class community that views the club with fierce local pride, it becomes particularly electric during south-Madrid derbies against Leganés and Rayo Vallecano.

name: Rayo Vallecano
description: The Estadio de Vallecas is a uniquely intimate 14,708-seat ground embedded in the tight streets of the Vallecas neighbourhood in south-east Madrid, where supporters stand barely metres from the pitch and the atmosphere is impossibly intense for a stadium of its scale. Rayo Vallecano's enduring reputation as a club of the people is embodied in every corner of this raw, unpretentious arena, which is beloved by football romantics across Spain and beyond.

name: RCD Mallorca
description: The Visit Mallorca Estadi, popularly known as Son Moix, is a 23,142-seat stadium on the Mediterranean island of Mallorca that has served as the club's home since 1999 and was substantially upgraded in subsequent years. Its open south end offers a unique backdrop of island sunshine and pine-clad hillsides, making it one of the most visually distinctive venues in La Liga and a compelling destination for football tourists.

name: Girona FC
description: Estadi Montilivi is a compact 13,450-seat ground in the historic Catalan city of Girona that has been the club's home since 1970 and became an unlikely stage for UEFA Champions League football when Girona made their historic European debut in 2024. The stadium's intimate dimensions and the feverish noise of the local support make every home fixture an electric occasion, ensuring visiting sides rarely find it a comfortable place to play.

name: Deportivo Alavés
description: The Estadio de Mendizorroza is a 19,800-seat ground in the Basque city of Vitoria-Gasteiz that has been the proud home of Deportivo Alavés since 1924, making it one of the oldest continuously used football venues in Spain. Surrounded by trees and woven into the city's residential fabric, the stadium generates a passionate community atmosphere that a loyal local fanbase punch well above their city's size to sustain.

name: CD Leganés
description: The Estadio Municipal de Butarque is a compact 11,454-seat ground in the southern Madrid suburb of Leganés, redeveloped in 2014 to meet La Liga standards and standing as a testament to a club that has fought its way up from the lower tiers of Spanish football. Small, loud, and fiercely partisan, Butarque is an especially hostile environment for visiting teams during south-Madrid derbies, when the local pride of the pepineros faithful is at its most intense.

name: RCD Espanyol
description: The RCDE Stadium is a sleek, modern 40,500-seat arena opened in 2009 in Cornellà de Llobregat on the south-western outskirts of Barcelona, giving Espanyol one of the most architecturally striking grounds in Spanish football. Its perfect circular geometry, sweeping continuous roof, and state-of-the-art facilities make it a formidable home fortress for the Pericos, particularly charged during high-stakes matches against city rivals Barcelona.

name: SD Eibar
description: Estadio Ipurua is one of the most extraordinary football grounds in the world, a 7,083-seat stadium perched on a steep Basque hillside in the small town of Eibar and hemmed in on all sides by apartment buildings and mountain terrain. The gravity-defying location, impossibly close and steep stands, and the fierce Basque support create an atmosphere that is utterly unique in professional football and irresistible to anyone who loves the game in its most authentic form.

name: Real Zaragoza
description: La Romareda is a 34,596-seat historic stadium in the centre of Zaragoza that has been the proud home of Real Zaragoza since 1957 and carries the memories of a club that was once among the most celebrated in Spanish and European football. Its traditional running-track oval design, the passionate maño supporters packed into the Fondo Norte terrace, and decades of storied history make it one of the most beloved and character-rich venues in La Liga.

name: Sporting Gijón
description: El Molinón is the oldest stadium in Spain still hosting professional football, having staged its first match in 1908 in the Asturian port city of Gijón, where the sport is woven into the identity of a proud working-class community. Expanded and renovated across more than a century of continuous use, the 29,029-seat ground retains a raw emotional power and genuine atmosphere that make following Sporting Gijón one of the most authentic experiences in Spanish football.
